fact: 1918年5月16日，美国国会通过《煽动法》（Sedition Act），作为对1917年《间谍法》的修正：新增9项罪名，包括对美国政府形式、宪法、国旗、军服发表「不忠、亵渎、粗鄙或辱骂性」言论，煽动削减战时生产，以及支持敌国事业；最高刑罚为1万美元罚金或20年监禁，或两者并罚。

sources.title: U.S. Government Publishing Office, Freedom of Speech in War Time（Senate document，含1918年5月16日修正条文列举）
sources.quote: On May 16, 1918, Congress amended the espionage act by what is sometimes called the sedition act, adding nine more offenses to the original three ... Whoever commits any one of these offenses in this or any future war is liable to a maximum penalty of $10,000 fine or 20 years' imprisonment, or both.

sources.title: HISTORY, U.S. Congress passes Sedition Act
sources.quote: Those who were found guilty of such actions, the act stated, shall be punished by a fine of not more than $10,000 or imprisonment for not more than twenty years, or both.

fact: 1918年6月，社会党领袖尤金·德布斯在俄亥俄州坎顿发表反战演说后被捕，依《煽动法》受审，被判10年监禁并被剥夺公民权；1919年最高法院维持原判。

sources.title: HISTORY, U.S. Congress passes Sedition Act
sources.quote: After delivering an anti-war speech in June 1918 in Canton, Ohio, Debs was arrested, tried and sentenced to 10 years in prison under the Sedition Act. Debs appealed the decision, and the case eventually reached the U.S. Supreme Court, where the court ruled Debs had acted with the intention of obstructing the war effort and upheld his conviction.

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, Sedition Act 40 Stat. 553 (1918)（Paul L. Murphy）
sources.quote: Enforced extensively in the period from May to November 1918, the measure virtually terminated wartime criticism until the Armistice.

Total bond allotments reached $6,992,927,100 and the total number of subscribers was 22,777,680.

sources.quote: An official communique was published by the United States at 2:30 pm: "In accordance with the terms of the Armistice, hostilities on the fronts of the American armies were suspended at eleven o'clock this morning."

fact: 美国零售物价在1918年上涨18%（1917年1月为10%、1919年1月为15%）；1916年12月至1920年6月物价以年化18.5%的速度上涨，累计涨幅超过80%，食品、服装与干货价格翻倍以上。

sources.title: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, One hundred years of price change: the Consumer Price Index and the American inflation experience, Monthly Labor Review, 2014（PDF）
sources.quote: The 12-month change in the CPI rose from 3.3 percent in January to double digits by October. The World War I era and its aftermath, 1917–1920, then produced sustained inflation unmatched in the nation anytime since. Prices rose at an 18.5-percent annualized rate from December 1916 to June 1920, increasing more than 80 percent during that period. ... The prices of most foods, clothing, and dry goods more than doubled.

fact: 1918年《煽动法》扩大了邮政总局局长的审查权：他可拒递任何「依《间谍法》不可投递」的邮件，并在信封上盖「Mail to this address undeliverable under the Espionage Act」字样退回；这一权力足以损坏个人或企业的生意与名誉。

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, Sedition Act 40 Stat. 553 (1918)（Paul L. Murphy, 1986）
sources.quote: The 1918 act also enlarged the censorship functions of the postmaster general, empowering him to refuse to deliver mail to any individual or business employing the mails in violation of the statute. He was to order a letter that he deemed undeliverable to be returned to the sender with the phrase "Mail to this address undeliverable under the Espionage Act" stamped on the envelope. Thus the postmaster general was empowered to damage or destroy the business or reputation of any American citizen.

fact: 纽约市的流感时间线：1918年8月11日挪威籍船 Bergensfjord 抵港，船上已有病人；9月15日记录首例流感死亡；10月4日单日新增999例，10月9日翻倍至2,000例，10月19日达4,875例；10月16日至26日每日死亡在400—500人之间。

sources.title: The New York Times, How New York Survived the Great Pandemic of 1918（Mike Wallace, 2020-03-20）
sources.quote: The virus arrived on Aug. 11, 1918, aboard the Norwegian vessel Bergensfjord. ... On Sept. 15 the first death from what was being called the Spanish influenza was recorded. ... On Oct. 4 physicians reported 999 new cases during the previous 24 hours. On Oct. 9 that doubled to 2,000. ... And on Oct. 19 4,875 new cases were tallied. ... Over 400 succumbed on Oct. 16, and the daily death count fluctuated between 400 to 500 from Oct. 16 to 26.

fact: 纽约市卫生专员科普兰没有关闭学校与剧院，理由是他认为学校「比许多城市住宅更清洁、更安全」，改用错峰上下班、商店16时关门、设立150多个紧急卫生中心、对随地吐痰者罚1美元；纽约的流感死亡率稳定在约4.7‰，低于波士顿的6.5‰与费城的7.3‰。

sources.title: The New York Times, How New York Survived the Great Pandemic of 1918
sources.quote: On Sept. 17, Royal S. Copeland, a homeopathic physician who in April had been appointed the city's health commissioner, required doctors to report instances of flu and pneumonia.

sources.title: Our Town, When It Was Worse
sources.quote: He convinced businesses to stagger their work shifts to avoid rush hour crowds, set up more than 150 emergency health centers across the city, put up posters telling residents to cover their coughs and sneezes in public, and told the police to slap $1 fines on people caught spitting. He did not, however, close schools ... New York's death rate stabilized at about 4.7 deaths for every 1000 people versus Boston's 6.5 and Philadelphia's 7.3. per 1,000.

fact: 1917至1918年美国船厂工人由5万人增至35万人以上，另有18万余人在钢厂与工厂预制部件；霍格岛船厂占地846英亩、有50个船台与250栋建筑，高峰雇工约3万人（一说3.4万人以上），平均每5.5天下水一艘船，共建122艘——但没有一艘在停战前投入服役。

sources.title: Naval History and Heritage Command, The First Dazzlers（PDF）
sources.quote: Between 1917 and 1918, the number of American shipyard workers grew from 50,000 to over 350,000, not including over 180,000 others making pre-assembled components at steel mills and plants around the country. ... Hog Island, the largest, had over 50 ship ways, 250 buildings, 100 miles of railway, and 28 outfitting docks located on 846 acres. At its peak, the shipyard employed more than 34,000 workers.

sources.title: Smithsonian National Postal Museum, Photograph of Hog Island（National Museum of American History 藏品说明）
sources.quote: At its peak, the yard employed around 30,000 workers. ... At its peak, Hog Island launched a vessel every 5½ days, and its workers built 122 cargo and troop transport ships in four years. Although none saw service before the end of the war, the United States learned how to build large ships quickly on a grand scale from prefabricated parts.
